title: Goods 10 - Road Haulage Operator Licensing and Market Access
source: Regulations (EC) 1071/2009 and 1072/2009 as amended by (EU) 2020/1055; RSA and Department of Transport guidance on the Road Haulage Operator Licence

questions.q: In Ireland, who needs a Road Haulage Operator's Licence?
options: Anyone carrying goods for reward in a vehicle over 3.5 t
Anyone driving any goods vehicle over 7.5 tonnes
Only hauliers who carry goods to other countries
Every company that owns a van or a lorry
questions.exp:
A Road Haulage Operator's Licence is needed to carry goods for hire or reward (someone else's goods, for payment) in a vehicle or combination with a maximum authorised weight over 3.5 tonnes.
📍 RSA / CVRT, Operator Licensing

questions.q: A builders' merchant delivers goods it has sold to its customers, in its own 18-tonne lorries driven by its employees. Does it need a road haulage licence?
options: Only if it crosses a border
Only if it charges for delivery separately
questions.exp:
Own-account work (your own goods, in your own vehicles, driven by you or your employees, including delivering goods a customer has bought from you) does not need a road haulage licence.
📍 RSA, Road transport operator licence

questions.q: What does 'hire or reward' mean for goods transport?
options: Carrying your own goods for free
Being paid to carry someone else's goods
Renting a lorry to a friend
Carrying goods between your own depots
questions.exp:
Hire or reward means carrying someone else's goods for payment. That is what triggers the need for a road haulage operator's licence.
📍 RSA / CVRT, Operator Licensing

questions.q: Which four requirements must a road haulage operator meet under Regulation (EC) 1071/2009?
options: Good repute, finance, competence and establishment
A Euro 6 fleet, a depot, a bank loan and a CPC
IRHA membership, insurance, a website and VAT
Ten years' experience, a yard and two vehicles
questions.exp:
The four EU requirements are good repute, appropriate financial standing, professional competence (a transport manager with the CPC) and an effective and stable establishment in the State. They must be met for as long as the licence is held.
📍 Regulation (EC) 1071/2009, Article 3

questions.q: What financial standing must a haulier show for heavy goods vehicles?
options: €5,000 for the first vehicle and €3,000 for each additional one
€9,000 for the first vehicle and €5,000 for each additional one
€12,000 for the first vehicle and €6,000 for each additional one
€1,800 for the first vehicle and €900 for each additional one
questions.exp:
Vehicles over 3.5 t: available capital and reserves of at least €9,000 for the first vehicle and €5,000 for each additional vehicle. (€1,800 and €900 are the amounts for light commercial vehicles.)
📍 Regulation (EC) 1071/2009, Article 7

questions.q: A haulier wants a licence for 6 heavy goods vehicles. How much financial standing must it show?
questions.exp:
€9,000 for the first vehicle + 5 × €5,000 for the others = €34,000.
📍 Regulation (EC) 1071/2009, Article 7

questions.q: Since 21 May 2022, which light commercial vehicles need an operator licence?
options: All vans used anywhere in Ireland
Vans over 2.5 t doing international paid work
Only electric vans used for deliveries
Only vans towing a trailer over 750 kg
questions.exp:
Under Regulation (EU) 2020/1055, operators using light commercial vehicles over 2.5 t (up to 3.5 t) for international hire or reward transport need a licence from 21 May 2022.
📍 Department of Transport, LCV international transport operations

questions.q: What financial standing is required for light commercial vehicles (2.5 to 3.5 tonnes) in international transport?
options: €900 for the first vehicle and €450 for each additional one
€1,800 for the first vehicle and €900 for each additional one
€9,000 for the first vehicle and €5,000 for each additional one
No financial standing is needed for vans
questions.exp:
For light commercial vehicles: €1,800 for the first vehicle and €900 for each additional vehicle.
📍 Department of Transport, LCV international transport operations

questions.q: Which body issues road haulage operator licences in Ireland?
options: The Department of Transport's RTOL unit
questions.exp:
Licences are issued by the Department of Transport's Road Transport Operator Licensing (RTOL) unit, through the rtol.ie portal. The NTA deals with bus route licences, not haulage.
📍 Department of Transport, road haulage operator licence

questions.q: For how long is an Irish road haulage operator licence normally valid?
questions.exp:
Licences are issued for up to five years and must then be renewed.
📍 Department of Transport; Road Traffic and Transport Act 2006

questions.q: Which certificate must a haulier hold to show it is up to date with its taxes when applying for a licence?
questions.exp:
Applicants must hold a valid tax clearance certificate, and good repute also requires Garda vetting and a self-declaration.
📍 Department of Transport, operator licence requirements

questions.q: What document allows an Irish haulier to carry goods for hire or reward between EU Member States?
questions.exp:
The Community Licence gives access to international road haulage within the EU. The original is kept at the operator's premises and a certified true copy is carried in each vehicle.
📍 Regulation (EC) 1072/2009, Article 4

questions.q: Where must a certified true copy of the Community Licence be kept?
options: In every vehicle on international work
At the RSA's head office in Ballina
At the customs office of the port
questions.exp:
The original stays at the operator's premises; a certified true copy must be carried in each vehicle and shown on request.
📍 Regulation (EC) 1072/2009, Article 4

questions.q: What is 'cabotage' in road haulage?
options: Haulage between two different EU countries by any haulier
Haulage inside another EU country by a foreign haulier
Haulage on a ferry, a train or any other vessel
Haulage of your own goods in your own company lorry
questions.exp:
Cabotage is national transport of goods for hire or reward carried out on a temporary basis in a host Member State by a haulier from another Member State.
📍 Regulation (EC) 1072/2009, Article 2

questions.q: After an international delivery into France, how many cabotage operations may an Irish lorry carry out there?
options: Up to 3 within 7 days of unloading
Up to 5 within 10 days of unloading
None: cabotage is banned in France
questions.exp:
Up to 3 cabotage operations within 7 days of the last unloading of the incoming international carriage.
📍 Regulation (EC) 1072/2009, Article 8, as amended by 2020/1055

questions.q: After a period of cabotage in a Member State, how long must the same vehicle wait before doing cabotage there again?
questions.exp:
Since 21 February 2022 there is a 4-day cooling-off period: the vehicle may not carry out cabotage with the same vehicle in that Member State for 4 days after the end of its cabotage period.
📍 Regulation (EC) 1072/2009, Article 8, as amended by 2020/1055

questions.q: Under the EU Mobility Package, how often must a vehicle used in international transport return to an operational centre in its home Member State?
options: Never: there is no such rule
questions.exp:
Since 21 February 2022, vehicles must return to one of the operational centres in the Member State of establishment within 8 weeks of leaving it.
📍 Regulation (EC) 1071/2009, Article 5, as amended by 2020/1055

questions.q: Under the Mobility Package, the operator must organise the work so that a driver can return home or to the operational centre:
options: Only at the end of the contract
questions.exp:
Drivers must be able to return home or to the employer's operational centre within each period of 4 consecutive weeks, or 3 weeks if two consecutive reduced weekly rests were taken.
📍 Regulation (EC) 561/2006, Article 8, as amended by 2020/1054

questions.q: Since 2 February 2022, drivers posted to another Member State for cabotage or cross-trade must be declared through:
questions.exp:
Posting rules apply to cabotage and cross-trade (not to bilateral trips to and from the home country). The operator files a posting declaration through the EU's IMI portal and the driver must be able to show it.
📍 Directive (EU) 2020/1057

questions.q: Which document lets a haulier carry goods to or through non-EU countries that belong to the International Transport Forum, such as Turkey or Serbia?
questions.exp:
ECMT (CEMT) multilateral permits, allocated in limited numbers by quota, cover journeys between member countries of the International Transport Forum; otherwise bilateral permits are needed.
📍 ITF / ECMT quota system

questions.q: A haulier from outside the EU employs a driver who is not an EU national. Which document must the driver carry for EU journeys?
questions.exp:
A driver attestation certifies that a non-EU driver is lawfully employed by the operator; it is issued by the Member State of establishment and carried with the certified copy of the Community Licence.
📍 Regulation (EC) 1072/2009, Article 5

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four requirements for a road haulage operator licence?
questions.exp:
The four requirements are good repute, financial standing, professional competence and establishment. Joining a trade association such as the IRHA is voluntary.
📍 Regulation (EC) 1071/2009, Article 3
